item.title: [VIDEO] Tinubu Departs Nigeria For Saudi Arabia To Perform Umrah
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has departed Abuja for Makkah, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, to perform Umrah, an Islamic spiritual exercise involving a pilgrimage to the Holy City. Tinubu departed at 2:20 p.m. on Thursday. The Special Adviser to the President on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, said in a statement on Wednesday that the visit would give the President an opportunity for spiritual reflection, devotion, and prayers for the nation’s peace, unity, stability, and continued progress. According to the statement, the President will perform the religious rites associated with Umrah, seeking Allah’s guidance and blessings for Nigeria and its people. Tinubu is expected back in the country next week upon the completion of the spiritual exercise. ﻿ The post [VIDEO] Tinubu Departs Nigeria For Saudi Arabia To Perform Umrah appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: INEC moves to tackle electoral risks in Abia
item.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has stepped up preparations for the 2027 general elections, with efforts to identify and address potential threats to peaceful and credible polls in Abia State. The Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in the state, Prof. Sylvia Agu, disclosed this on Thursday in Umuahia at a stakeholder sensitisation workshop on Electoral Risk Management (ERM). Agu said early identification of electoral threats, effective coordination and collaboration among stakeholders were critical to preventing disruptions and strengthening public confidence in the electoral process. “Successful elections require deliberate preparation, effective coordination and the collective commitment of all institutions and individuals involved in the electoral process,” she said. She urged stakeholders, particularly security agencies, to sustain their cooperation with INEC to ensure peaceful elections and strengthen democracy. The Abia State Commissioner of Police, CP Wilfred Olutokunbo Afolabi, also reaffirmed the police commitment to credible elections. Represented by the Deputy Commissioner of Police in charge of Operations, DCP Ifeanyi Uzor, Afolabi said the police would protect election materials, provide security for National Youth Service Corps members and ensure a safe environment for voters. “The 2027 election will not be an exception. We have a renewed commitment from the Inspector-General of Police to ensure credible elections in 2027. That duty we must perform without fear or prejudice,” he said. Also speaking, the INEC Administrative Secretary in Abia, Chief Ama Agwu, said the ERM framework would help identify, assess and manage security threats, political tensions, environmental challenges and operational difficulties capable of disrupting elections. Agwu urged electoral officers to ensure that information gathered was accurate, verified and reflective of conditions on the ground to facilitate timely interventions. Earlier, the Head of the Department of Planning and Monitoring, Mr Ogbuisi Robinson, said the workshop was designed to identify electoral risks specific to Abia, strengthen early-warning and response mechanisms, and promote evidence-based planning. He said the exercise would also involve collaboration with the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES). INEC officials, including Electoral Officers from all 17 local government areas in Abia, representatives of security agencies and other stakeholders attended the workshop. item.title: ICPC docks alleged ‘fake’ PFIPC DG Adeyemi for forgery, impersonation
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Abuja The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) on Thursday arraigned the self-styled Director-General (DG) of the alleged “non-existent” Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council (PFIPC), Prince Adeniyi Adeyemi, on a 22-count charge relating to forgery and impersonation. Adeyemi, who has been in detention since July 14, was docked before Justice Halilu Yusuf of the High Court of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) sitting in Maitama. The ICPC alleged that the defendant, while passing himself off as a public servant, obtained over N27 billion to start the fake agency. He was also alleged to have dubiously obtained another N3.8 billion for personnel costs. The prosecution told the court that Adeyemi also obtained funds through a forged document addressed to the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy. It alleged that the defendant forged documents purportedly signed by the Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, which he claimed appointed him Director-General of PFIPC, and used them to occupy government office facilities at the Federal Secretariat Complex Phase III, Abuja. Besides, Adeyemi was accused of forging a document addressed to the Accountant-General of the Federation, captioned “RE: REQUEST FOR APPROVAL OF SELF-ACCOUNTING STATUS”, for the non-existent agency to operate within the government financial reporting structure. He was said to have forwarded forged documents to the DG of the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) to get a domain name for the agency. The defendant was also accused of gifting N210,000, without official authorisation, to one Aminu Abdullahi, an Assistant Chief Technical Officer in the Office of the Secretary General of the Federation (OSGF), “to facilitate the allocation of office space.” He allegedly gifted another N300,000 to Ogaba Harry, an officer in the Office of the Chief Economic Adviser to the President, to facilitate the release and handover of two official vehicles, a Prado SUV and a Land Cruiser SUV, to him. Other counts in the charge included an allegation that on July 29, 2025, the defendant collected N20 million from one Oyekunle Gbenga, the Managing Director of Divine Dopacy Nigeria Limited, under the false pretence of a “project facilitation loan” for a purported N2.8 billion contract allegedly awarded by the fictitious agency for the procurement of furniture and renovation of the official residence of the DG of the said non-existent PFIPC. The ICPC insisted that he committed the offences between 2024 and 2026. He was said to have contravened Sections 364, 366 and 132 of the Penal Code Cap. 532, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria (Abuja) 1990; Section 1(1)(a) of the Advance Fee Fraud and Other Fraud Related Offences Act, 2006, punishable under Section 1(3); and Section 9(a) of the Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Act, 2000, punishable under Section 9(b). item.title: Trump says Brazil election was ‘a disgrace’
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Thursday stepped up criticism of Brazil’s “disgraceful” election, declining to say whether he recognized leftist Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva as president after right-wing rival Flavio Bolsonaro claimed victory. “I think the election was a disgrace in Brazil,” Trump told reporters when asked if he accepted Lula’s victory, a day after his ally Bolsonaro fled to the United States and proclaimed himself the rightful leader. “I don’t want to comment on it right now, but I thought the election was a very great embarrassment to the people of Brazil… I thought it was a very disgraceful situation for Brazil.” The post Trump says Brazil election was ‘a disgrace’ appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Digital divide could become new colonialism — Russia warns
item.description: … Offers AI research partnership to Africa By Nkiruka Nnorom Russia has warned that unregulated development of Artificial Intelligence, AI, risks deepening global inequality and creating a new form of colonialism, with Africa at risk of becoming a raw-material appendage of the AI economy. The warning was issued by Andrey Akulchev, Acting Director of Department of International Information Security of Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, at the session “AI as a Factor in Development of Russia and Africa: Science and Personnel” held as part of business programme of third Russia-Africa Economic and Humanitarian Forum in Moscow. “If development of artificial intelligence is left unregulated, digital divide could become a new global watershed and fertile ground for modern forms of colonialism,” Akulchev said. According to him, Russia advocates equal access to technology and takes the interests of countries of Global South into account. “Africa must not become either a raw-material appendage of the new AI-based economy or a free data warehouse for those who train their models on it,” he stated. Akulchev disclosed that within framework of Russia-Africa summit, a separate declaration on AI has been agreed, which enshrines right of each country to independently determine its policy in this area and supports multilingual solutions, including Swahili, Yoruba, Hausa, Amharic and Zulu. Also speaking at same session, First Deputy Minister of Economic Development of Russian Federation, Maxim Kolesnikov, said Russia has been supporting 13 research centres in the field of artificial intelligence, where more than 2,000 scientists work since 2021. He said the centres are open to cooperation with African colleagues. “We also invite our African colleagues to cooperate on basis of our laboratories. Together with foreign scientists from our centres, as well as foreign partner centres from 36 countries, we held International AI Foresight last year,” Kolesnikov said. He noted that one of the preparatory sessions of the foresight was held in Morocco with participation of representatives of African countries. Both interventions formed part of broader push by Moscow to position AI cooperation as pillar of Russia-Africa partnership, anchored on technological sovereignty, local capacity building and respect for national regulatory autonomy, rather than one-way technology transfer. item.title: Reps seek urgent action as Taraba attack toll hits 60
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has called for urgent security and humanitarian intervention following a bandit attack on Binnari community in Karim Lamido Local Government Area of Taraba State, which reportedly left between 57 and 60 people dead. The attack occurred on October 23, 2026, when residents and traders gathered at the community market, according to a motion moved on Thursday by Mohammed Audu, who represents Karim Lamido, Lau and Ardo Kola Federal Constituency. Audu told the House that the assailants opened fire on the market, killing 10 people instantly, while panic reportedly caused several others to jump into a river, bringing the estimated death toll to between 57 and 60. He described the incident as unprecedented in the area and called for immediate measures to prevent further attacks and provide relief to affected communities. The lawmaker disclosed that the attackers returned on October 26 to neighbouring Gomben Dela community, where they allegedly looted food items and seized vehicles before fleeing. No deaths were reported in the second incident. Audu identified forested areas in Plateau and Bauchi states, including Dutsen Zaki in Wase Local Government Area, Kukawa Forest in Kanam Local Government Area, and locations around Yankari Government Reserve and Gwana Mountain in Alkaleri Local Government Area, as possible routes used by the attackers. He said the forested areas shared boundaries with communities in Karim Lamido, making stronger cooperation among security agencies in the three states necessary. The lawmaker also expressed concern over the poor road network linking affected communities, urging the Federal Ministry of Works to complete the abandoned Wase-Karim Lamido road project to improve access for security personnel and facilitate emergency response. Following deliberations, the House called on the Federal Government to strengthen intelligence-sharing among security agencies in Taraba, Plateau and Bauchi states to prevent a recurrence of the attacks. It also urged the North-East Development Commission, National Emergency Management Agency, National Commission for Refugees, Migrants and Internally Displaced Persons, and other humanitarian organisations to provide food, building materials, blankets, mattresses and other relief supplies to affected families and survivors. The lawmakers observed a minute of silence in honour of those killed and commended the Taraba State governor, military commanders, the state Commissioner of Police, the Director of the Department of State Services and other security agencies for their response to the incident. item.title: Edo Queens miss CAF Women’s Champions League after controversial WAFU-B final replay
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Nigeria Women’s Football League (NWFL) champions, Edo Queens, have lost their place in the 2026 CAF Women’s Champions League after suffering a 3-2 defeat to Ghana’s Ampem Darkoa Ladies in a controversial replay of the WAFU-B qualifying final in Cairo, Egypt, on Thursday. Mohammed Afishata scored in the 92nd minute to hand Ampem Darkoa victory after the match resumed from the beginning of extra time, following a ruling by the Confederation of African Football (CAF). Edo Queens had initially won the September 5 final in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso, after the match ended 2-2 in regulation time and they triumphed in the ensuing penalty shootout. However, CAF later nullified the result after ruling that the match officials had wrongly proceeded directly to penalties without playing the mandatory 30 minutes of extra time. Following an appeal by Ampem Darkoa, CAF ordered that the omitted extra time be played, with the score restored to 2-2. The replay took place in Cairo on Thursday, with Ampem Darkoa taking advantage of the opportunity to score early in extra time and secure a 3-2 victory, ending Edo Queens’ hopes of qualifying for the continental competition. Edo Queens made two changes to their team for the resumed match, bringing in Kafayat Mafisere and Mary Mamudu for Oluwakemi Adegbuyi and Oluebube Umejiaku, who were away on national duty. The Nigerian champions, however, failed to find a late equaliser as the Ghanaian side held on to secure qualification. The victory gives Ampem Darkoa their second appearance at the CAF Women’s Champions League, having last featured in the competition in 2023 in Côte d’Ivoire. The Ghanaian club will compete in Group B alongside defending champions AS FAR of Morocco, USFAS Bamako of Mali and Kawempe Muslim Ladies of Uganda. Edo Queens, who reached the semi-finals on their debut in 2024, will miss this year’s tournament following the defeat. The 2026 CAF Women’s Champions League is scheduled to hold in Egypt from November 1 to 15. item.title: Carrick not surprised he’s still Man Utd manager
item.description: Under-pressure Manchester United manager Michael Carrick said Thursday he was “here to do my job” as he insisted he needed “no assurances” over his future at Old Trafford. Carrick also said he was unsurprised to still be in charge after a woeful run of results and gave his backing to United captain Bruno Fernandes. Portugal midfielder Fernandes was left on the bench for last week’s loss at home to Bournemouth following his criticism of Carrick’s tactics in a 4-1 thrashing by Como. Carrick’s position has been the subject of intense speculation after a miserable run of eight games without a win. Sunday’s 3-0 humbling loss at home to Bournemouth left the English giants one point above the Premier League relegation zone. United have won just two of 12 matches in all competitions this season, with a return of seven points from eight league games representing their worst start to a league season in 40 years. But Carrick remains in charge and, speaking ahead of Saturday’s match away to Chelsea, the 45-year-old former United and England midfielder was in defiant mood. Asked if he was still surprised to be in post, he told reporters: “No. I’m here to do my job. I’m here to do the best for the team. I’m desperate to make things better and improve things. I’m not surprised, no.” – ‘Get the position’ – Carrick was equally adamant he did not require public backing from the United hierarchy. “I don’t need assurances from anyone,” he said. “I totally get the position, I get the job, the responsibility, I get what comes with that.” Questioned on Fernandes’s position, Carrick said leaving him on the bench against Bournemouth was a “decision for the game”. “That’s it. Bruno is fully committed to this football club. I’ve got no issues with that, we move forward. We’re looking forward to the game at the weekend now.” Carrick appears to have the backing of the United faithful, being warmly applauded by fans as he made his way down the tunnel following the defeat by Bournemouth. Moments later a chorus of boos erupted as the players left the pitch as supporters made clear where they think the blame lies for United’s poor performances. Nevertheless, former United captain Gary Neville, who played alongside Carrick at Old Trafford said earlier Thursday that “sometimes a manager needs sacking for their own good”. But Carrick was adamant he would not walk away from his job. “I genuinely don’t take any notice of anything else. I know this job and I know what we need to be better. I don’t need anyone else to tell me…I’ve said it before, I care about what the supporters think…I care about what we give them and what they see.” And he insisted his much criticised players cared, too. “The boys are hungry,” he said. “We’re hurting because we haven’t won enough football games. But there is an intensity, an edge, a hunger to do better.” AFP The post Carrick not surprised he’s still Man Utd manager appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: PANDEF demands 50% oil derivation for Niger Delta
item.description: By Daniel Abia PORT HARCOURT — The Pan Niger Delta Elders Forum (PANDEF) has called on the Federal Government to increase the derivation allocation to oil-producing states from the current minimum of 13 per cent to 50 per cent, citing environmental degradation and the developmental challenges facing the region. The group also urged the government to invest in modular refineries to complement existing refining facilities, while insisting that the completion of the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway and East-West Road projects must not be compromised. The demands were contained in a 48-point communiqué jointly signed by former Akwa Ibom State Governor, Obong Victor Attah, Chairman of PANDEF’s Board of Trustees, and its National Chairman, Dr. Godknows Boladei Igali. The communiqué followed a virtual meeting of the Board of Trustees and National Executive Committee of the forum on Tuesday. PANDEF noted that Section 162(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, provides for the allocation of not less than 13 per cent of revenue accruing directly from natural resources to states from which the resources are derived. It argued that the provision had remained unchanged for more than two decades, despite the environmental damage, ecological challenges and developmental burdens borne by oil-producing communities in the Niger Delta. “PANDEF therefore calls for an increase in the derivation allocation from the current minimum of 13% to a minimum of 50%, to enable oil-producing communities and states to address the longstanding developmental deficits, environmental damage, health hazards and social and economic consequences of oil and gas exploration and production,” the communiqué stated. The forum also challenged presidential candidates of various political parties to demonstrate their commitment to environmental justice by presenting practical, measurable and time-bound plans for cleaning up and restoring affected communities. It said communities across the Niger Delta continued to suffer the consequences of pollution, ecosystem damage and loss of livelihoods after more than six decades of oil and gas exploration and production. PANDEF called for urgent intervention in affected areas, including Nembe Creek in Bayelsa State, Odidi in Delta State and Kula in Rivers State. It also demanded adequate, sustained and transparent funding for the Ogoni cleanup programme, urging the Federal Government to develop a comprehensive framework for extending environmental remediation to other parts of the Niger Delta. Coastal highway, East-West Road On infrastructure, PANDEF welcomed the Federal Government’s decision to retain the original broad alignment of the 750-kilometre Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway as a distinct strategic project, following reported reconsideration of a proposal to integrate the route into the East-West Road. item.title: 2027: Makinde targets jobs, manufacturing in APM agenda
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike The Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has promised to prioritise job creation, skills training and manufacturing as part of his party’s agenda for Nigeria, with its manifesto scheduled for unveiling on November 4. Makinde spoke at the APM South-East town hall meeting in Enugu, where he said the party had consulted Nigerians across the six geopolitical zones to develop solutions to unemployment, poverty, insecurity and the trust deficit between leaders and citizens. Makinde said the party’s agenda rested on four pillars: economic recovery, security restructuring, education reform and a reset of the sociopolitical space. “We do not simply manufacture policies out of thin air. We listen to our people, hear what they want to see, and incorporate their expectations into our agenda,” Makinde said. The governor disclosed that the party had partnered with Skill Reset Nigeria to train one million young Nigerians in skills intended to improve their employment prospects. He also identified high interest rates and inadequate access to long-term financing as major obstacles to manufacturing, promising to create a business environment that would encourage entrepreneurship and sustainable job creation. Makinde urged Nigerians to reject religious and ethnic divisions, arguing that the country’s challenges affected everyone. “Our message to you today is this: Please reject all forms of division along religious or ethnic lines. The challenges we face do not discriminate on the basis of religion or ethnicity,” he said. The governor also criticised President Bola Tinubu’s planned trip to Saudi Arabia to pray for Nigeria, saying leaders should combine prayers with honesty and action at home. “Prayers can also be answered here in Nigeria. Please, we will remain here, pray for our country and pray for our leaders because Nigeria belongs to all of us,” Makinde said. He urged supporters to protect their Permanent Voter Cards and use them in the 2027 election, alleging that political opponents were distributing money to buy support and destroying the party’s campaign materials. “Let them pull down our posters. Let them destroy our billboards. But please, keep your Permanent Voter Cards and be ready to use them to vote. They cannot take your thumbprints away from you. That is what you will use to send them out of power,” he said. The APM National Chairman, Yusuf Dantalle, called on Tinubu to withdraw from the 2027 presidential race and support Makinde, citing the Oyo governor’s reported support for the President in 2023. “Today, we are calling on President Tinubu to support a new direction and step aside, withdraw from the 2027 race to allow Makinde complete remaining four years Southern term,” Dantalle said. item.title: Nigeria borrows to build, not to bridge fiscal gaps – Tinubu
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has said Nigeria is shifting from borrowing to cover short-term fiscal pressures to raising funds for infrastructure projects that can drive economic growth, create jobs and support the country’s ambition of becoming a $1 trillion economy by 2030. Tinubu said the government’s economic reforms had improved the country’s fiscal position and strengthened its access to international capital, but stressed that the next phase must focus on completing projects and delivering measurable benefits to Nigerians. The President stated this in an article titled “From Reforms to Delivery: Our Infrastructure Investment and Growth Strategy,” shared on X on Thursday by his Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga. He said the removal of petrol subsidy, exchange-rate unification and tax reforms had helped restore macroeconomic balance and improve government revenue. According to Tinubu, Nigeria’s real gross domestic product growth reached 4.43 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, while headline inflation fell to 14.63 per cent in September from 20.98 per cent a year earlier. He also said gross external reserves stood at $55.1bn as of October 9, 2026, including about $46bn in net reserves. “These reforms have restored macro balance, quadrupled federation revenue since 2021 and rebuilt the credibility of the State’s balance sheet,” Tinubu wrote. He argued that the improved fiscal position should enable the government to channel more borrowing towards productive investments while maintaining financial discipline. “Borrowing to build, not to bridge, not for consumption: Nigeria is fundamentally changing the purpose of public borrowing: from financing short-term fiscal pressures to investing in assets that will transform the economy for generations,” he said. Tinubu said public debt stood at 35.75 per cent of GDP in the second quarter of 2026, while debt servicing consumed about 65 per cent of revenue in the first half of the year. He acknowledged the need for fiscal discipline, stating that the Federal Executive Council’s economic strategy ruled out deficit monetisation and unfunded commitments during the pre-election period. The President listed the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway, Trans-Sahara Superhighway, electricity grid improvements and upgrades to commercial ports in Lagos among the administration’s priority infrastructure projects. He said the projects would connect economic regions, improve access to markets, reduce logistics costs and attract private investment. Tinubu cited progress on the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, saying that as of August 2026, Lot 2 was reported to be more than 80 per cent complete, while work on the Calabar-Akwa Ibom section was over 30 per cent complete. item.title: NAFDAC destroys N8bn fake, banned products in North-Central
item.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has seized and destroyed fake, adulterated, expired and banned products worth more than ₦8 billion across North-Central Nigeria. The Director-General of NAFDAC, Prof. Mojisola Adeyeye, disclosed this on Thursday in Lafia, Nasarawa State, saying the products were confiscated from manufacturing facilities, sales outlets, markets and motor parks across the zone. Adeyeye, who was represented by a Deputy Director of the agency in the zone, Joseph Edor, said the bulk of the destroyed products comprised banned alcoholic beverages packaged in sachets and containers smaller than 200 millilitres. She explained that the restriction on alcoholic beverages in sachets and glass bottles below 200ml was introduced because their affordability, availability and portability made them susceptible to abuse, particularly among young people and underage schoolchildren. According to her, early exposure to alcohol can affect brain development and damage vital organs, including the liver and kidneys. “Research has shown that early exposure to alcohol affects the brain and other vital organs such as the liver and kidneys,” she said. She added that alcohol consumption among children could contribute to impaired brain development, poor academic performance, reduced productivity and other health complications. Adeyeye said NAFDAC was established under Decree No. 19 of 1993, as amended, with the responsibility of protecting public health by ensuring that regulated products manufactured, imported, distributed and sold in Nigeria meet the required quality and safety standards. She said the ban on certain alcoholic beverages and the subsequent enforcement operations were aimed at curbing abuse, addiction and associated health risks. Other items seized during the operations included expired and counterfeit medicines, as well as adulterated and unwholesome food products and cosmetics. The director-general commended law enforcement agencies, sister agencies and other stakeholders for supporting NAFDAC’s operations through intelligence sharing and the provision of security. The Nasarawa State Coordinator of NAFDAC, Dr. Gyani Stephen, said the exercise was intended to protect public health rather than harm traders or businesses. She warned dealers in counterfeit and banned products to desist from the practice, adding that the agency would take legal action against offenders. In a goodwill message, the Nasarawa State Commander of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency, Daniel Saidu, represented by Yakubu Awoh, commended NAFDAC for its efforts to protect lives through the seizure and destruction of expired and counterfeit products. item.title: Obi promises emergency measures on security, corruption, poverty
item.description: Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr Peter Obi, has promised emergency measures to tackle insecurity, corruption, hunger and poverty, if elected. Obi made the promise on Thursday during an interactive town hall meeting with a large crowd of supporters across party lines in Abakaliki. The former Anambra governor said that Nigeria required purposeful leadership to achieve sustainable development, adding that he possessed the character, experience and capacity to lead the country. He said that Nigeria had vast arable land and other resources that could transform its economy if properly harnessed. According to him, the country must shift from consumption to production, particularly through agriculture and other productive sectors. On the Federal Government’s borrowing, Obi said taking loans was not inherently wrong but became problematic when the funds were used for consumption rather than productive investments. “It becomes wrong when the government borrows to buy a yacht or a presidential plane for consumption purposes,” he said. He pledged that his administration would ensure transparency in public borrowing, insisting that Nigerians must know why loans were obtained and how the funds would be utilised. On security, the presidential candidate promised to deploy modern technology and other effective measures to tackle insecurity and guarantee the safety of citizens across the country, irrespective of their locations. Obi also vowed that anyone found guilty of corruption, including the president, would face prosecution and imprisonment in accordance with the law. He said his vision was to build a Nigeria where citizens could achieve their aspirations through merit rather than personal connections. “My dream is to see a Nigeria where the son of a nobody can become somebody without knowing anybody,” he added. Obi, who expressed excitement over the turnout at the meeting, described himself as the most credible among the three leading presidential candidates. He cited President Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress (APC), former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and himself as the leading contenders. He urged Nigerians to participate actively in the forthcoming election and protect their votes. “You should vote for me because I am the most credible candidate among the leading candidates for the presidency,” he said. Obi expressed optimism that Nigeria could achieve meaningful transformation under credible leadership, pledging to provide such leadership if elected. item.title: Nursing mother drags husband to court over N10,000 ‘breastfeeding allowance’
item.description: A nursing mother, Firdausi Ahmad on Thursday dragged her husband, Malam Anas before a Shari’a Court in Kaduna, seeking divorce and N10,000 monthly for “breastfeeding” allowance. The ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‌‍​‌‌⁠⁠​‌​complainant’s lawyer, Malam Sani Sunusi, told the court that his client had been married to Anas for three years and she was nursing an eight months old daughter. The counsel told the court that his client’s husband, told her to go back to her parents house until he gives her approval to return to their matrimonial home. “Since my client went to her parents, the defendant never checked on her or their eight months old baby. “My client prays the court to dissolve the marriage through Khul’i and is willing to return his dowry of N100,000. “He should also pay N10,000 monthly for the baby’s needs and for the eight months that she’ll be breastfeeding her baby” he prayed. The defendant was not in court. The Judge, Malam Yakubu Abdullahi, adjourned the case until Nov. 11 for the complainant to present her witness or evidence. Abdullahi directed the registrar of the court to send a letter of invitation to the defendant and ensure that he attends the hearing. item.title: Makinde questions Tinubu’s Saudi prayer trip, challenges FG over borrowing
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has questioned the Federal Government’s decision to seek fresh foreign loans despite rising external reserves and claims of improved revenue collection. Makinde spoke on Thursday at the party’s South-East town hall meeting in Enugu, where he also criticised President Bola Tinubu’s planned trip to Saudi Arabia to pray for Nigeria, urging the government to be transparent about the country’s economic situation. “I was reading on social media yesterday night up until this morning that our president is travelling to Saudi Arabia to pray for Nigeria. Prayers are answered even in this country; we will stay here, and we will pray for Nigeria and also our leaders because Nigeria belongs to all of us,” he said. Makinde’s comments came after the President’s Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, announced on Wednesday that Tinubu would travel to Makkah on Thursday to perform Umrah, an Islamic pilgrimage, and pray for Nigeria’s peace, unity, stability, and continued progress. The president subsequently departed for the trip on Thursday. Makinde urged the president and his administration to address the country’s challenges honestly, saying prayers should be accompanied by transparency about the state of the economy. “They should pray for Nigeria and stop all the deceit and tell Nigerians the exact true situation of things so that as you are praying, our prayers will not be in vain,” he said. The Oyo State governor also questioned the government’s decision to seek additional borrowing despite claims of improved revenue collection and the country’s growing external reserves. Vanguard reported that President Tinubu recently, in a letter to the Senate, sought the approval of a supplementary external borrowing plan of about $20.52bn and €1.045bn to finance infrastructure and development projects across the country. “They said we have a lot of money in our external reserve and that the Nigeria Revenue Service has surpassed the target for the year, but we still have to go and borrow money. How does it add up?” Makinde asked. He said his experience in the private sector had taught him to assess economic performance by the availability of long-term financing for businesses. “I came from the private sector; at the age of 29, I have paid salaries for workers till today. So, I know when the economy is expanding. One of the indications is that within your economy space you will have long-term facilities,” he said. Makinde added that businesses were largely relying on short-term credit facilities, which he said limited their ability to expand manufacturing and create jobs. He argued that manufacturers could not grow sufficiently when they had to borrow at interest rates of about 25 per cent without access to long-term financing. item.title: Video: Tinubu departs Abuja for Saudi Arabia to perform Umrah
item.description: President Bola Tinubu on Thursday departed Abuja for Makkah, Saudi Arabia, to perform Umrah, an Islamic pilgrimage to the holy city. The presidential aircraft, an Airbus A330-200, took off at 2:20pm local time, with the president expected to return to Nigeria next week after completing the religious exercise. Tinubu was seen off at the airport by six governors: AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq of Kwara, Babagana Zulum of Borno, Uba Sani of Kaduna, Ahmad Aliyu of Sokoto, Umar Namadi of Jigawa and Mai Mala Buni of Yobe. Also present were the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, George Akume; the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi; and Nigeria’s Ambassador to Mexico, Reno Omokri, alongside other government officials. The President’s departure was announced on Thursday by his Special Assistant on Social Media, Dada Olusegun, in a post on X. Olusegun said the visit would give Tinubu an opportunity for spiritual reflection and prayer for Nigeria. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu departs Abuja for Makkah, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, to perform Umrah, the Islamic spiritual exercise involving a pilgrimage to the Holy City. The visit gives the President an opportunity for spiritual reflection, devotion, and prayers for Nigeria’s… pic.twitter.com/QFSEFfqpB1 — Daddy D.O (@DOlusegun) October 29, 2026 “The visit gives the President an opportunity for spiritual reflection, devotion, and prayers for Nigeria’s peace, unity, stability, and continued progress,” he wrote. He added that the President would perform the religious rites associated with Umrah while seeking divine guidance for the country. “While in Makkah, President Tinubu will perform the religious rites associated with Umrah, seeking Allah’s guidance and blessings for Nigeria and its people,” Olusegun said. Thursday’s trip marks the second time Tinubu has travelled to Makkah to perform Umrah since assuming office on May 29, 2023. The President visited the holy city in November 2023, shortly after attending the Saudi-African Summit in Riyadh, where he also prayed for divine guidance in leading Nigeria. The latest trip is part of a series of foreign engagements undertaken by Tinubu since becoming president. He has visited more than 30 countries in over 50 unique and recurring trips. item.title: N70,000 Allowance: ‘Negotiate your terms,’ NLC tells TUC
item.description: Joe Ajaero, President of the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, has asked the Trade Union Congress, TUC, to negotiate its terms with the Federal Government, as it cannot reject the N70,000 transport allowance NLC agreed with government for public sector workers. Vanguard reported that TUC rejected the proposed N70,000 monthly transport allowance for federal workers, which NLC agreed upon after a meeting. According to TUC, the federal government has the resources to pay N300,000. In a statement by Festus Osifo and Nuhu Toro, President-General and Secretary, respectively, the TUC said in view of the prevailing economic hardship facing workers and the wider population, as well as the proposed measures to address it, what was needed was a salary increase and the implementation of the Joint Health Sector Union, JOHESU, agreement. Read the full story HERE . Responding in an interview on Channels TV on Thursday, Ajaero, NLC President, said officials of the TUC did not negotiate with the federal government on the subject. He described TUC’s position on the allowance as improper. He noted that the leadership of the TUC does not have the power to reject the agreement terms of a sister-agency. The NLC president said: “I would have preferred a situation whereby if NLC was asking for one Naira, TUC will be asking for 10 Naira. “TUC never asked for intervention as a result of the rising cost of transportation. On the issue of asking for wage increase, does the government gift wage increase? There must be a process put in place. “I’m worried for some time now why you will say you reject something that was not given to you. That is not proper. “You don’t have the power to reject what a sister agency negotiates. You have the power to ask for your own.” Vanguard News The post N70,000 Allowance: ‘Negotiate your terms,’ NLC tells TUC appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Tinubu made life expensive, Atiku’ll make it affordable — Akobundu
item.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — The Director-General of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Austin Akobundu, has criticised President Bola Tinubu’s economic policies, saying former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar would prioritise affordability and economic recovery if elected president in 2027. Akobundu spoke during the inauguration of the Atiku/Akobundu Vanguard, a grassroots mobilisation group, in Ikwuano and Umuahia North Local Government Areas of Abia State. The senator, who is also the ADC candidate for Abia Central Senatorial District, expressed confidence in the prospects of Atiku and other party candidates in the 2027 elections, citing what he described as growing public support. “Tinubu has made life expensive for Nigerians. Atiku will make life affordable again for the people,” he said. Akobundu said Atiku’s economic proposals, including the restoration of targeted subsidies, would help ease financial pressures on Nigerians and support economic recovery. He also highlighted the former vice-president’s positions on national unity and equal opportunities, arguing that the proposed revival of the Eastern maritime port corridor could stimulate trade, investment and economic activities in the South-East. The senator urged Nigerians, particularly those in the South-East, to support Atiku, whom he described as capable of improving living conditions and strengthening the economy. He further urged the region to look beyond political sentiments, arguing that Atiku’s presidency could create opportunities for a Nigerian of Igbo extraction to emerge as president in the future. Constituency projects, legislative interventions Akobundu also highlighted his legislative activities and constituency projects in Ikwuano and Umuahia North, including efforts to attract federal institutions, youth empowerment programmes, scholarships, student grants, healthcare interventions and infrastructure development. He cited his intervention on the delayed rehabilitation of the Umuahia–Ikot Ekpene Federal Road, saying the Senate had acted on his motion before the Abia State Government took over the reconstruction under a refund arrangement with the Federal Government. The senator commended Governor Alex Otti for taking over the project and the quality of work carried out, while acknowledging the contributions of former lawmaker, Rep. Sam Onuigbo, to efforts to secure the road’s rehabilitation. “I do not play politics of division and bitterness. That road is for our people, and anyone who contributes to its reconstruction deserves commendation,” he said. Youth empowerment, education The senator listed scholarships, student grants, vocational training and digital skills development among his human capital development initiatives. He said the programmes included grants of ₦200,000 each to 114 tertiary students and three-year scholarships valued at ₦21 million for 113 constituents studying at the National Teachers Institute. item.title: ‘Horrific’ Russian Drone Strike Kills 14 At Ukraine Train Station
item.description: A Russian drone slammed into a busy platform at a railway station in Ukraine’s Dnipro on Thursday killing at least 14 people in what President Volodymyr Zelensky called a “horrific” attack that demands a response from Kyiv’s allies. The strike came as Ukraine and Russia strive to uphold a fragile local ceasefire in the ravaged city of Oleshky — under Russian occupation since 2022 and where residents have faced months of food, water and medicine shortages. The truce was holding into its third day, both countries said, with the Ukrainian human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets announcing that he had “set out with the Ukrainian delegation towards Oleshky” through Belarus and Russia. But elsewhere, Moscow continued to pummel Ukraine. The strike at the Dnipro train station hit a platform “where a regular commuter train and a regular passenger train were standing”, Zelensky said. By early Thursday afternoon, Dnipropetrovsk regional governor Oleksandr Ganzha said the death toll from the strike had risen to 14. EDITORS NOTE: Graphic content / In this handout photograph taken and released by the Ukrainian Emergency Service on October 29, 2026, Ukrainian law enforcement officers work at the site of an air attack on the railway station in Dnipro, amid the Russian invasion of Ukraine. (Photo by Handout / UKRAINIAN EMERGENCY SERVICE / AFP) Another 14 had been wounded, he said, adding that six of them were in severe condition after suffering “multiple shrapnel wounds”, including an 11-year-old boy and a man who had “both legs amputated”. Zelensky slammed the attack as “horrific” and insisted that “sanctions against Moscow and its war machine must not be eased for as long as this Russian war continues”. Images released by Ukrainian emergency services showed bodies on the platform, rescuers helping victims to safety and two burnt-out passenger trains with their windows shattered. French President Emmanuel Macron reacted with outrage to the attack, stressing the need for “far more than a localised ceasefire” like the one in Oleshky. “It is intolerable that Russia continues to reject all proposals to this end, choosing instead to pursue escalation and target civilians,” he said on X. Zelensky slams sanctions relief Russia has fired drones on trains across Ukraine since the first days of its 2022 invasion — destroying hundreds of locomotives and killing several railway workers. Ukraine’s air force said it had intercepted three jet-powered drones in a daytime attack, but that a fourth evaded its defences and hit the station. In the aftermath of the attack, Zelensky refreshed his criticism of a deal struck this month between US President Donald Trump and his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin to ease some sanctions on Russia allowing Moscow to release diesel onto global markets. “How many such terrorist strikes has Russia carried out against our people since sanctions were lifted on some Russian oligarchs and the energy sector, instead of de-escalating,” he asked. item.title: Indonesians Celebrate Rain After Months Of Smoke And Suffering
item.description: Residents and firefighters in an Indonesian city long shrouded in a toxic haze brought on by months of wildfires rushed outside dancing and chanting as rain this week brought a welcome respite. On Wednesday night, exhausted volunteer firefighters jumped around in the puddles and kissed the ground in gratitude as another burst came down. “We were overjoyed; every one of us volunteers was so happy that we prostrated ourselves in gratitude. Praise be to God that there was finally rain,” firefighter Lukman El Hakim told AFP. TOPSHOT – Indonesian soldiers, tasked with fighting forest and land fires, celebrate as it rains in Banjar Baru, South Kalimantan province on October 28, 2026, following months of forest and land fires. (Photo by MUDA SAGALA / AFP) | MUDA SAGALA / AFP Intermittent rains have been falling in Palangkaraya, the capital of Central Kalimantan province on Indonesian Borneo, where devastating wildfires have raged since August. The city’s air quality index hit 4,000 this month, its worst ever measurement and more than 13 times the environment ministry’s threshold for pollution deemed “hazardous” to health. More than 11,000 people have been treated for respiratory infections in Palangkaraya during the months-long crisis that has also affected Indonesia’s neighbours with haze pollution. The World Health Organisation has linked exposure to air pollution, including high levels of tiny, airborne PM2.5 particles, to increased risk of illness and premature death. A volunteer (R) assists a woman with a nasal oxygen cannula at a shelter run by the Central Kalimantan Forest and Land Fire Smoke Response Coalition (RAKAT) to aid residents experiencing respiratory difficulties in Palangkaraya, Central Kalimantan.More than 11,000 people have been treated for respiratory infections in Palangkaraya during a months-long wildfire crisis. At least 11 people have died fighting Indonesia’s wildfires, most recently a 45-year-old forest ranger who was killed by a falling tree while battling flames in North Toraja, South Sulawesi, on Wednesday. Palangkaraya resident Muhammad Jihan Alwi used the reprieve to jog outdoors for the first time in months. “Of course I’m happy to be out jogging again, breathing in fresh air that’s better than yesterday, just feeling grateful,” the 23-year-old said, smiling. item.title: Five Things To Know Today
item.description: TUC rejects ₦70,000 transport allowance as proposed scheme could cost ₦465.7 billion The Trade Union Congress has rejected the Federal Government’s temporary ₦70,000 monthly transport allowance for federal workers, demanding a permanent salary increase instead. President Bola Tinubu during the inauguration of the APC PCC. The government agreed with the Nigeria Labour Congress on Tuesday to provide the allowance for six months, beginning in November. However, a Punch analysis estimates that the programme could cost ₦465.7 billion over six months if all 1.1 million employee records on the federal payroll qualify. This is an estimate, not an officially approved expenditure figure. TUC President Festus Osifo argues that earlier temporary wage awards were inconsistently implemented and failed to reach many eligible workers. Why it matters: What appeared to be a breakthrough in labour negotiations has exposed disagreement within organised labour. The government must now address both the affordability of its proposed intervention and workers’ demands for permanent improvements in income. Watch: The government’s response to the TUC, final eligibility rules, the funding source and whether the NLC–government agreement proceeds as scheduled. INEC meets today to decide fate of Pantami, Adebutu and other excluded candidates INEC The Independent National Electoral Commission is considering petitions from parties whose governorship candidates were excluded from its published list for the February 6, 2027 elections. INEC National Commissioner Mohammed Haruna confirmed that the commission would examine the matter at today’s meeting. Affected candidates include Isa Pantami of the PDP in Gombe, Ladi Adebutu of the PDP in Ogun and Aminu Gwarzo of the Nigeria Democratic Congress in Kano. Several exclusions followed disputes over party nominations and compliance with membership-register requirements under the Electoral Act. No final decision from today’s meeting had been verified at this editorial cut-off. Why it matters: The commission’s decisions could determine which candidates appear on governorship ballots and whether additional court challenges become necessary. Watch: INEC’s formal decisions, publication of corrected candidate lists and legal responses from affected parties. States leave ₦264 billion in basic education funds unused A new investigation published today reveals that state governments had ₦264.12 billion in unspent Universal Basic Education Commission matching grants, according to UBEC’s 2025 Annual Report. The balances were recorded during financial monitoring visits conducted as of July 21, 2025. Benue accounted for ₦19.18 billion, Imo ₦14.12 billion, Osun ₦14.02 billion, Kwara ₦13.99 billion and Delta ₦13.40 billion. The findings come amid continuing reports of deteriorating classrooms, overcrowding and inadequate school facilities.
